papers.summary: The operation of next-generation wireless networks increasingly hinges on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize critical network decisions. papers.title: Distributed Collaborative Positioning through ISAC for GPS-Denied Robotic Swarms
papers.summary: Robotic swarms in GPS-denied environments require accurate position and velocity in real-time for all nodes, without external infrastructure or centralized control. papers.summary: This paper investigates the Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) framework under individual penalty constraints to address resource allocation challenges in dynamic wireless networked environments. papers.summary: Few-shot coverage and capacity optimization (CCO) under a small adjustment budget is challenging: model-based methods suffer from simulator mismatch, while feedback-based methods are sample-starved. papers.summary: Adaptive urban traffic signal control must coordinate motorized traffic, public transport, cyclists, and pedestrians under heterogeneous and highly dynamic demand. papers.summary: In this work, integration of scheduling and control is approached through a multi‐decision Deep Reinforcement Learning agent that simultaneously performs scheduling and control actions in a reactive fashion in chemical batch plants. Due to the complexity in batch processes, multiple techniques are proposed to enhance the policy training. A heuristic‐based policy was developed using knowledge of the objectives and constraints of both tasks. A dataset was built and used for supervised pretraining of the agent's networks. papers.title: Robust adaptive model-free tracking control via ACRL-based dynamic gains FOESO of LIM drive for transportation systems applications
papers.summary: This article proposes a robust adaptive model-free tracking control (RAMFTC) based on actor-critic reinforcement learning (ACRL) for a linear induction motor (LIM) drive to achieve high-dynamic performance in transportation systems. Owing to the uncertainties, friction forces, parameter disparities, and exterior disturbances that exist in the LIM drive system, the design of a model-based controller cannot achieve this control purpose. The RAMFTC scheme incorporates a model-free integral sliding-mode controller (MF-FOISMC) and a dynamic gains fractional-order extended state observer (DG-FOESO).
